# Bandwidth
> Bandwidth is a global cloud communications software company that helps enterprises deliver exceptional experiences through voice calling, text messaging and emergency services. Our solutions and our Communications Cloud are trusted by companies like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Cisco, Google, Microsoft, RingCentral, Zoom, Genesys, Five9, and Uber. Bandwidth is the first and only CPaaS provider offering a unique combination of composable APIs, AI capabilities, owner-operated network and broad regulatory experience.

## Glossary

- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/model-context-protocol-mcp/): Learn what MCP means, and why the Model Context Protocol standard is important for CPaaS companies and API-leveraging platforms.
- [What is a Webhook?](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/webhook/): Discover what a webhook is and how it enables seamless communication between applications. Learn how webhooks work and their benefits alongside traditional APIs.
- [API key](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/api-key/): What is an API key? Learn how these unique identifiers authenticate API access, track usage, and the essential security best practices you need to follow.
- [Endpoint](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/endpoint/): Learn what an Endpoint is in the context of telecommunications and its role in managing network communications effectively.
- [Endpoint identifier](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/endpoint-identifier/): Discover the importance of an Endpoint Identifier and how it uniquely distinguishes devices in telecom networks.
- [Master Street Address Guide (MSAG)](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/master-street-address-guide-msag/): Discover what an MSAG is and how it enhances 911 call routing with accurate street and address data. Learn more about the Master Street Address Guide today.
- [Application Program Interface (API)](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/application-program-interface-api/): Application Programming Interface (API) is a set of subroutine definitions, protocols, and tools for building application software.
- [Call routing](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/call-routing/): Call Routing is the act of delivering communications from an originating source to the desired terminating endpoint including voice and data communications.
- [Group messaging](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/group-messaging/): What is group messaging? Group messaging is an SMS conversation between 3+ recipients simultaneously. Bandwidth offers a ready-to-use API for group messaging
- [Local Exchange Routing Guide (LERG)](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/local-exchange-routing-guide-lerg/): LERG (Local Exchange Routing Guide): Managed by Telcordia, the LERG contains key telecom routing data. Learn more with Bandwidth.
- [Messaging API](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/messaging-api/): Learn what a Messaging API is and how it powers seamless communication in applications. Explore its features, benefits, and implementation strategies from Bandwidth.
- [Phone call API / Voice calling API](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/phone-call-api-voice-calling-api/): Phone Call API / Voice Calling API is an API that lets developers easily integrate voice functions like automated call control into an application.
- [Coder-Decoder (Codec)](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/coder-decoder-codec/): Codec (Coder-Decoder) is used to encode audio from an analog signal to digital so that it can be passed across a data network. Learn what a codec does in this 101 glossary guide.
- [HTTP Voice](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/http-voice/): HTTP Voice is a voice call that originates and terminates over HTTP using a codec that will support voice calling. Bandwidth provides voice calling via API.
- [Message callback](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/message-callback/): Message Callback is the ability to setup a webhook or http callback to notify your server of a message event, like message received or message delivered.
- [REST APIs](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/rest-api/): A RESTful API uses HTTP requests to GET, PUT, POST and DELETE data. Using a REST API with callbacks (or webhooks) allows for a robust API model.
- [Voice Callback](https://www.bandwidth.com/glossary/voice-callback/): What is a callback? Voice Callback is the ability to set up a webHook or http callback to notify your server of a call event. Learn more.
